framework.name: expo
framework.notes: Expo SDK 57 + React Native 0.86 + React 19.2.3, expo-router file-based routing (typedRoutes + reactCompiler experiments on, app.json), NativeWind 4 for styling. FIRST-PASS CORRECTION: this is NOT react-vite — there is no vite/webpack/react-dom app, no index.html app shell and no `vite` script; package.json main is 'expo-router/entry' and the only web target is app.json web.output='server'. Also: default branch is 'master', not 'main'. Server code is Expo Router API routes (src/app/api/*+api.ts) under web.output='server', intended for EAS Hosting (PLAN.md A8).

monorepo.notes: Single Expo app at repo root; no workspaces key in package.json, no packages//apps/ dirs.

auth.notes: @clerk/expo v4 (useSSO, useAuth) on the client; @clerk/backend verifyToken guards API routes (src/lib/server-auth.ts) and createClerkClient deletes the Clerk user on account deletion; Clerk -> Trigger.dev webhook at src/app/api/webhooks/clerk+api.ts (svix signature + idempotency keys). Single role, no admin/teams — PLAN.md says explicitly no admin, no sharing. Native Google/Apple SSO requires an EAS dev build, not Expo Go. DATABASE_URL + CLERK_SECRET_KEY are hard-required: src/db/index.ts and src/lib/server-auth.ts throw when unset.

env.notes: Names come from the README .env block; there is no .env.example in the tree. Code only reads 5 of them: EXPO_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (src/app/_layout.tsx, throws on boot if missing) and server-side CLERK_SECRET_KEY, CLERK_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET, DATABASE_URL, IMAGEKIT_SECRET_KEY. OPENAI_API_KEY and TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY are read by the openai / @trigger.dev SDKs, not by name in the source. SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN is consumed by the @sentry/react-native/expo config plugin (app.json) and getSentryExpoConfig (metro.config.js) during native build / sourcemap upload, hence the build-time entry. IMAGEKIT_PUBLIC_KEY and IMAGEKIT_URL_ENDPOINT are dead names (see pitfalls). No environment variable VALUES appear anywhere in tracked files.

deploy.notes: No Dockerfile, no compose, no CI, no build script in package.json (scripts are start/android/ios/web/lint/db:*). Native dirs /ios and /android are gitignored (Expo CNG prebuild) so the mobile app is built via `npx expo run:ios|android` locally or EAS. API routes only exist as Expo Router server routes (app.json web.output='server'), which PLAN.md A8/R4 ties to EAS Hosting with a documented fallback to a standalone Hono server; Trigger.dev tasks deploy to Trigger.dev cloud from trigger.config.ts. app.json does not set the expo-router `origin`, which src/lib/api.ts says a production build needs for relative fetch('/api/...') calls.

tests.notes: The only test-like artifact is src/lib/plan.check.ts — a self-check script run with `node --experimental-strip-types src/lib/plan.check.ts` (node:assert/strict, asserts the Mifflin-St Jeor math, the AI-plan validator and the zod trust boundary); tsconfig explicitly excludes '**/*.check.ts'. No jest/vitest/playwright/testing-library in dependencies, no .github directory, and PLAN.md A8 states the project intentionally has 'no staging, no CI/CD'.

vendor.name: clerk
vendor.what_it_does: auth, sessions, JWT verification, user lifecycle webhooks
vendor.swap_target_hint: better-auth (with the Expo/native plugin) or Supabase auth

vendor.name: neon
vendor.what_it_does: managed Postgres over HTTP (drizzle-orm/neon-http driver, casing snake_case)
vendor.swap_target_hint: any Postgres (Supabase/RDS/self-hosted) — swap the driver to node-postgres

vendor.name: openai
vendor.what_it_does: vision meal recognition (photo -> calories/macros) and AI daily-target generation, both via Responses API + zodTextFormat structured outputs, model gpt-5.6-luna
vendor.swap_target_hint: any vision LLM with structured output (Anthropic/Gemini) or an on-prem model

vendor.name: trigger.dev
vendor.what_it_does: background jobs with retries + Realtime run subscriptions (tasks: analyze-meal, generate-plan, clerk-user-created/updated/deleted)
vendor.swap_target_hint: in-house queue (BullMQ/pg-boss) for the jobs plus SSE/websocket for scan status — the deepest lock-in in the repo

vendor.name: imagekit
vendor.what_it_does: meal photo storage + resize transform + batch delete by filename prefix on account deletion

vendor.name: sentry
vendor.what_it_does: error tracking, structured logs, sourcemap upload, in-app debug screen

vendor.name: expo-eas
vendor.what_it_does: native build/dev-client + the only documented host for the API routes (EAS Hosting)
vendor.swap_target_hint: port the 4 route handlers to a standalone Node/Hono host (PLAN.md R4 fallback)

pitfalls.detail: Expo SDK 57 / RN 0.86 mobile app: /ios and /android are gitignored and never committed, so there is no server-style `install && run`. README's `npx expo run:ios|android` needs Xcode or the Android SDK locally and @clerk/expo's Google/Apple SSO needs an EAS dev build (Expo Go will not do). PLAN.md line 203: 'Create the EAS dev build early — Apple/Google credentials, bundle IDs. Do not defer this.'
pitfalls.evidence: README.md Run the App section + .gitignore (/ios, /android) + app.json plugins [@clerk/expo] + PLAN.md

pitfalls.detail: Server code throws at import when its key is unset: src/db/index.ts ('DATABASE_URL is not set'), src/lib/server-auth.ts ('Add CLERK_SECRET_KEY'), src/lib/imagekit.ts ('Add IMAGEKIT_SECRET_KEY'). Any API route or Trigger.dev task needs DATABASE_URL + CLERK_SECRET_KEY + IMAGEKIT_SECRET_KEY + TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY + OPENAI_API_KEY present before anything works.

The README .env block lists IMAGEKIT_PUBLIC_KEY and IMAGEKIT_URL_ENDPOINT, which no code path reads (all ImageKit traffic is server-side with the private key). Copying the README list verbatim adds two dead variables.
pitfalls.evidence: README.md .env block vs grep for IMAGEKIT across every fetched src/**/*.ts|tsx — only IMAGEKIT_SECRET_KEY appears, in src/lib/imagekit.ts

pitfalls.detail: src/lib/api.ts says a production build needs `origin` on the expo-router plugin in app.json pointing at the deployment; app.json lists "expo-router" with no options, so relative fetch('/api/...') calls in a native production build have no base URL. A fresh agent will watch the app hang on 'analyzing' before finding this.
pitfalls.evidence: app.json plugins[] (bare "expo-router" entry) + src/lib/api.ts header comment

pitfalls.detail: legal/ is an unwired static site: store badges href='#', every mailto: is empty, terms contains placeholders and example.com, and _headers keeps the whole thing noindex 'until the docs are final'. src/app/debug-sentry.tsx is a Sentry test screen reachable in the app tree.
pitfalls.evidence: legal/index.html hrefs (mailto:, href="#"), legal/terms.html placeholder/example.com lines, legal/_headers, src/app/debug-sentry.tsx

pitfalls.detail: metro.config.js carries three hand-written resolver workarounds: a `browser` condition fallback for @trigger.dev/react-hooks' deps (nanoid/jose have no react-native key), dropping @s2-dev/streamstore's 'transport/s2s' import for Hermes, and a bugsnag/cuid '#fingerprint' special case. Bumping Trigger.dev or Clerk can silently break the native bundle — the file itself warns 'Expo HAS CHANGED' (AGENTS.md) about SDK 57.

Tightly pinned ecosystem: React 19.2.3 + RN 0.86.0 + expo ~57.0.8 + expo-router typed routes + reactCompiler experiment + NativeWind 4 on Tailwind 3 + TypeScript ~6.0.3. package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 3) is the only known-good combination — expect peer conflicts if any of these are bumped independently.

8 transitive packages declare install scripts in the lockfile (@sentry/cli, esbuild ×3, core-js, browser-tabs-lock, fsevents, unrs-resolver). Checked because a postinstall is the usual delivery vector: every one of the 1386 'resolved' entries points at https://registry.npmjs.org, none at a custom host, and package.json itself declares no install scripts.
pitfalls.evidence: package-lock.json 'hasInstallScript' entries + `grep resolved` host histogram (1386/1386 registry.npmjs.org)

verdict.best_for: A mobile-first AI photo logger: it is a genuinely functional product skeleton (anonymous onboarding -> AI-generated calorie/macro targets -> camera scan -> daily log with streaks and account deletion) for a consumer health, fitness or any-photo-logged app on iOS/Android.
verdict.weak_for: Anything web-first, self-hosted or needing maintenance: the API exists only as Expo Router server routes aimed at EAS Hosting, it cannot run until four paid vendor accounts (Clerk, Neon, Trigger.dev, ImageKit) exist, and it is explicitly a course build — PLAN.md says 'This is a tutorial/course build', one author wrote all 10 commits over 10 days (2026-07-25 to 2026-08-04), there is no CI, no issue history and a single self-check file instead of a test suite.
verdict.swap_burden: heavy — four coupled vendors (Clerk auth, Neon Postgres + Drizzle, Trigger.dev jobs + Realtime, ImageKit storage) are wired through routes, tasks and screens, and with no CI or tests nothing will catch a botched swap.

Real deployment state: no homepage field, no releases, no tags and no store URLs in the repo, so whether the app was ever published to the App Store / Google Play (the landing page implies it) could not be determined from the repo.

Node engine requirement: package.json has no engines field and there is no .nvmrc/.node-version; README only implies a Node capable of `--experimental-strip-types` for the check script and the drizzle-kit CLI.

Exact LOC: loc_estimate is a line count of the fetched src/**/*.ts|tsx + scripts/*.ts files (3917 lines) rounded; no cloc/tokei run and the static legal HTML/CSS (~2500 lines) and 2.7 MB of assets are excluded.
Contributor share: GitHub reports exactly one contributor (burakorkmez, 10 commits = 100%), but commit authorship for the 29 forks and any private collaboration is not measurable from the API.
